decisions.reason: The buzzer prototype and sourcing decision does not change which power rails are monitored or the INA3221 monitoring configuration.
The source changes only the acceptable passive-buzzer part and sourcing flexibility, not any interboard connector, pinout, or power-distribution rule.
The shared voltage and LCSC terms are incidental; the passive-buzzer choice does not alter the selected LED, its supply voltage, or its data interface.
Accepting an alternative production buzzer does not change the standalone USB supply, its powered rail, or source-selection behavior.
The buzzer part-selection decision does not change DCDC1 output voltage, current rating, compensation, or rail-stability requirements.
The source does not assign the buzzer to the switchable 5V rail or change the boost converter's loads, enable control, or operating policy.
The passive-buzzer sourcing decision is unrelated to the SPS30 connector, supply, and I2C-mode interface.
The source does not change USB enumeration, flashing, connector sourceability, or USB data routing.
The buzzer component is not identified as part of the sensor-board connector fanout, and no connector count or assignment is changed.
The acceptable buzzer alternative does not change the selected ESP32-S3 module or its LCSC part number.
The source records sourcing flexibility for the buzzer Requirement but does not change the existing power-board BOM-readiness attributes or identify a required modification to that BOM.
The passive-buzzer component choice does not change the AXP2101 battery input, normal-operation power source, or load-coverage rule.
